newsitem.title: UK: Halifax float fuels shares in bank sector.
newsitem.headline: Halifax float fuels shares in bank sector.

text.p: The flotation of the Halifax Plc which began its first day of trading at an indicated 774-1/2p, fuelled share price rises across the banking sector.
Abbey National shares rose 22p to 904p, NatWest gained 21p to reach 770, and the Lloyds TSB Group gained 16p to 630p.

The Halifax announced strong auction results before the stockmarket opened, showing a bidding range of 710 to 815p and an average price of 732.5p achieved for around 570 million shares or 23 percent of the group.

Shares in Barclays Plc were up 12p at 1196p, Royal Bank of Scotland gained 12p to 611 and Standard Chartered 11-1/2 to 987. The Abbey National, the first building society to convert into a bank in 1989, gained 13p to 893p.
Some 7.6 million Halifax members became shareholders in the flotation. The Halifax guaranteed shareholders selling their entitlement at auction will receive at least 415 pence per share.

Analysts had forecast the share price would be between 650p and 720p while an opening price of 774-1/2p valued the group at around 19.4 billion stg, making it the 16th largest listed UK company in terms of market capitalisation.

Until today the Halifax, like Britain's other building societies, has been owned by its savers and borrowers -- known as its members. Last February they voted in favour of a proposal for their society to convert to a public limited company and float on the stock exchange.
